resources.string: A close-up of normal articular hyaline cartilage. Molecules and matrix regions are simplified, and slow matrix maintenance is shown on a shortened timescale.

The chondrocyte occupies a small space called a lacuna. The pericellular matrix hugs the cell, the territorial matrix surrounds that rim, and the interterritorial matrix fills the space between cells.
The chondrocyte releases type II collagen precursors. Outside the cell, collagen assembles into fibrils that join the existing network. Collagen in mature cartilage is very slow to turn over.
The cell also makes and releases aggrecan. These brush-shaped molecules attach to hyaluronan strands outside the cell, replenishing aggregates within the collagen network.
Aggrecan has negatively charged side chains that help draw water into the matrix. The collagen network restrains swelling, so the hydrated matrix can resist compression.

Brief pressure squeezes the matrix and shifts some of its water. When pressure lifts, water moves back and the tissue recovers its shape. This is much faster than the cell’s ongoing matrix maintenance.
